DILG Republic of the Philippines DEPARTMENT OF THE INTERIOR AND LOCAL GOVERNMENT DILG-NAPOLCOM Center, EDSA corner Quezon Avenue, West Triangle, Quezon City http: //www.dilg.com.ph DILG OPINION No. 87 s. 2022 AUG 26 2022 ENGR. ZAMZAMIN L. AMPATUAN Undersecretary for Regulations and Infrastructure Department of Agriculture 2F DA Main Building, Elliptical Road Diliman, Quezon City Dear Usec. Ampatuan: This refers to your proposal to create a plantilla position in the Department of Agriculture which will be referred as Barangay Agricultural Extension Worker (BAEW) and Bantay Bayan Para sa Masaganang Ani (BBM Ani) to be assigned in barangay or clustered barangays in the country, or alternatively, to be funded by the barangay to be supported by the DA, contained in your Memorandum dated 6 July 2022, addressed to President Ferdinand R. Marcos, Jr., thru Executive Secretary, Atty. Victor D. Rodriguez. This Department commends the efforts of the Department of Agriculture to bridge the gap in providing sustainable link between the National Government and LGUs in terms of information affecting the agriculture industry of our country. The DA is empowered to promulgate and enforce all laws, rules and regulations governing the conservation and proper utilization of agricultural resourcesl. As such, creation of position as proposed, may be allowed. However, at this time, creation of plantilla positions at the barangay level may not be feasible as the DA is already in partnership with the Municipal Agriculturists for the endeavored thrust since it is the latter's mandate to promote agricultural development and growth. The Municipal Agriculturist's function is to initiate and extend technical assistance to farmers so they can develop plans and strategies for farming rice, corn, fruits, vegetables, and high-valued crops. Moreover, the position may not be readily available for barangays that are not in the nature or classified as agriculture. May we also present our additional observations/comments: A. EMPLOYMENT CLASSIFICATION May we inquire on the type of employment classification the DA opts to consider since the letter request provided that it is seeking to create a plantilla position but it seemed that the hired applicant will be under a contractual appointment or contract of service/job order. 1 Section 3(3), Chapter l, Title IV of Executive Order No. 292 or the Administrative Code of 1987 "Matino, Mahusay at Maaasahan" Trunkline No.: 8876-34-54

Employment status differs in terms of duration, nature of work, and benefits. Therefore, it is important to provide the classification of the employee prior to hiring. A Permanent Employment/Plantilla Position is issued to a person who meets all the minimum qualification requirements of the position to which he is being appointed, including the appropriate eligibility prescribed in accordance with the provisions of law, rules, and standards promulgated in pursuance thereof. This includes all levels of positions . They may be provided full benefits under the law. Under the 2016 Omnibus Rules on Appointments and Other Human Resource Actions, Rule.lV, Section l, a contractual appointment is issued to a person whose employment in the government is in accordance with a special contract to undertake local or foreign assisted projects or a specific work or job requiring special or technical skills not available in the employing agency, to be accomplished within a specified period. The inclusive period of the contractual appointment shall be indicated on the face of the appointment for purposes of crediting services. Employees under contractual appointment must meet the education, training and experience requirements of the positions as proposed by the respective Agency Heads and approved by the Commission. Eligibility is not required for appointment, except those whose duties involve the practice of a profession regulated by the Philippine Bar/Board or special laws and/or require licenses such as those positions listed under category IV of CSC MC No. 11, s. 1996 as amended, but preference should be given to civil service eligibles. Contractual appointments are limited to one year, but may be renewed every year, based on performance, until the completion of the project or specific work. Contract of Service (COS) refers to the engagement of the services of an individual, private firm, other government agency, non-governmental agency or international organization as consultant, learning service provider or technical expert to undertake special project or job within a specific period while a Job Order (JO) refers to piece work* (pakyaw) or intermittent or emergency jobs such as clearing of debris on the roads, canals, waterways, etc. after natural/ man-made disasters/occurrences and other manual/trades and crafts services such as carpentry, plumbing, electrical and the like. These jobs are of short duration and for a specific piece of work COS workers shall be paid the prevailing market rates while individuals hired.through JO shall be paid wages equivalent to the daily wage/salary of comparable positions in government and a premium of up to 20% of such wage/salary. B. REQUIREMENTS FOR THE CREATION OF THE POSITION Per letter request, funding or budget allocation may either be sourced from the barangay or the DA Regional Office, however distinction should be made since there are different procedural and reportorial requirements for the creation of such. a. Plantilla position Under the Department of Agriculture (DA) or Under the Local Government Unit (LGU) Page 2 of 4

a. 1. kequirements for the Creation of a New Title under the DA 1. Agency request endorse by the Department/Agency Head 2. Legal Basis, if applicable; 3. Rationale/Justifications of the Proposal 4. Description of the positions involved, which would include the following: 4.1. Number of Positions; 4.2. Position title/salary grade/unique item number, as necessary; 4.3. Functions/duties/responsibilities of the proposed positions; 4.4. Funding status, as necessary; 4.5. Organizational Deployment of the Proposed Positions; 4.6. Projected Workload and Schedule of operations of the units where the proposed positions would be deployed; 4.7. Computation of the annual PS Cost of the proposed positions; and 4.8. Similar Filled Items (Permanent/Casual/Contractual) in the unit concerned. a.2. Requirements for the creation of New Class Titte/Position for LGUs; 1. Letter-Request of the Local Chief Executive (LCE); 2. Justification for the Creation of the Class Title/Position; 3. Duly Accomplished Position Description Form (PDF) for each position; 4. Organizational Chart; 5. Position Allocation List by Department/Division/Unit; 6. Functions of each Department/Division/Unit, with emphasis on the Unit where the position to be created will be deployed; 7. Sanggunian Resolution Creating the New Position/s; and 8. Appropriation Ordinance providing funds for the creation of new position/s; 9. Certification from the Local Budget Officer/Local Finance Committee that the PS cap/limitation has not been exceeded despite the creation. b. Contractual Appointment Contractual personnel or those whose employment in the government is in accordance with a special contract to undertake a specific work or job, requiring special or technical skills not available in the employing agency, to be accomplished within a specific period, which in no case shall exceed one year. c. Individual Contract of Service The individual contract of service requires the execution of either a contract of services or Memorandum of Agreement (MOA) or job order between the government agency concerned and the individual, in accordance with the rules and regulations prescribed by the Commission on Audit. The Contract of Services, MOA or job order shall not contain the following provisions: 1. The employee performs work or a regular function that is necessary and essential to the agency concerned or work also performed by the regular personnel of the hiring agency; Page 3 of 4

2. The employee is required to report to the office and render service during the agency's prescribed office hours from 8:00 am to 5:00 pm or for forty (40) hours per week; 3. The employee is entitled to benefits enjoyed by govemment employees such as ACA, PERA and RATA and other benefits given by the agency such as mid-year bonus, productivity incentive, Christmas bonus and cash gifts. 4. The employee's conduct and performance shall be under the direct control and supervision of the government agency concerned; and 5. The employee's performance shall be evaluated by the government agency. On the aspect that the employee will be under the supervision and control of the Municipal Agriculturist, the Local Government Code of 1991 states that the position of the agriculturist shall be mandatory for the provincial govemment and optional for the city and municipal govemments2. Hence, not all municipalities/cities have Agriculturist. Lastly, since the herein proposal involves creation of position, inputs/comments of the Civil Service Commission (CSC) and Department of Budget and Management (DBM) should be solicited as they are responsible in assessing and evaluating the following: (1) Minimum qualification; (2) Nature/Status of Appointment (whether plantillla or contract of service); (3) Compensation/Emoluments; and (4) Budget and Funding requirement. Thank you. Very respectfully yours, BY AUTHORITY OF THE SECRETARY: MAR Unders GAN ry for Local Government LLLS/RPB/LRALLD/rrao/clp copy HON. LORAJEAN A.
